text.brief: A college student in Seattle binges a mainland drama in 2040 about a reformer who saves the nation from corrupt rivals. The show costs nothing, looks superb and draws its money from one faction of a Party at war with itself.
text.record: Ne Zha 2 earned about $2.26 billion worldwide in 2025 and about $23 million in North America. A Beijing-based publisher listed in Shenzhen owns 49 percent of the company behind ReelShort, a short-drama app that earned about $130 million worldwide in the first quarter of 2025. Short dramas reach American audiences through phones rather than theaters.
text.reading: A weakened faction courts the world with beauty. Its dramas, games and idols carry a story in which that faction saves the nation, and viewers abroad become its constituency. This is Stratagem 31, the beauty trap.
text.coreEvent: A streaming channel funded by one Party faction draws more than 50 million monthly viewers outside the mainland before 2045.
text.gapText: Application Architecture. App stores name the developer of a show and not the state faction that paid for it.
text.fix: Label the ultimate sponsor of state-backed foreign media in every app store.
